text: As we express our gratitude, we must never forget that the highest appreciation is not to utter words, but to live by them.
author: John F. Kennedy

text: Gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all the others.
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero

text: Happiness cannot be traveled to, owned, earned, worn or consumed. Happiness is the spiritual experience of living every minute with love, grace, and gratitude.
author: Denis Waitley

text: Gratitude is the healthiest of all human emotions. The more you express gratitude for what you have, the more likely you will have even more to express gratitude for.
author: Zig Ziglar

text: Feeling gratitude and not expressing it is like wrapping a present and not giving it.
author: William Arthur Ward

text: One looks back with appreciation to the brilliant teachers, but with gratitude to those who touched our human feelings. The curriculum is so much necessary raw material, but warmth is the vital element for the growing plant and for the soul of the child.
author: Carl Jung

text: I am happy because I'm grateful. I choose to be grateful. That gratitude allows me to be happy.
author: Will Arnett

text: Gratitude is the fairest blossom which springs from the soul.
author: Henry Ward Beecher

text: 'Thank you' is the best prayer that anyone could say. I say that one a lot. Thank you expresses extreme gratitude, humility, understanding.
author: Alice Walker

text: Gratitude is the sign of noble souls.
author: Aesop

text: We learned about gratitude and humility - that so many people had a hand in our success, from the teachers who inspired us to the janitors who kept our school clean... and we were taught to value everyone's contribution and treat everyone with respect.
author: Michelle Obama

text: If having a soul means being able to feel love and loyalty and gratitude, then animals are better off than a lot of humans.
author: James Herriot

text: I don't have to chase extraordinary moments to find happiness - it's right in front of me if I'm paying attention and practicing gratitude.
author: Brene Brown

text: Everything we do should be a result of our gratitude for what God has done for us.
author: Lauryn Hill

text: Gratitude is one of the strongest and most transformative states of being. It shifts your perspective from lack to abundance and allows you to focus on the good in your life, which in turn pulls more goodness into your reality.
author: Jen Sincero

text: I would maintain that thanks are the highest form of thought, and that gratitude is happiness doubled by wonder.
author: Gilbert K. Chesterton

text: Gratitude is riches. Complaint is poverty.
author: Doris Day

text: Never lose the childlike wonder. Show gratitude... Don't complain; just work harder... Never give up.
author: Randy Pausch

text: There is only one thing that can form a bond between men, and that is gratitude... we cannot give someone else greater power over us than we have ourselves.
author: Montesquieu

text: The discipline of gratitude is the explicit effort to acknowledge that all I am and have is given to me as a gift of love, a gift to be celebrated with joy.
author: Henri Nouwen

text: I live by two words: tenacity and gratitude.
author: Henry Winkler

text: When you have balance in your life, work becomes an entirely different experience. There is a passion that moves you to a whole new level of fulfillment and gratitude, and that's when you can do your best... for yourself and for others.
author: Cara Delevingne

text: I acknowledge my feeling and gratitude for life by praising the world and whoever made all these things.
author: Mary Oliver

text: It is always easier to requite an injury than a service: gratitude is a burden, but revenge is found to pay.
author: Tacitus

text: Gratitude, warm, sincere, intense, when it takes possession of the bosom, fills the soul to overflowing and scarce leaves room for any other sentiment or thought.
author: John Quincy Adams

text: I am of the African race, and in the colour which is natural to them of the deepest dye; and it is under a sense of the most profound gratitude to the Supreme Ruler of the Universe.
author: Benjamin Banneker

text: On the recollection of so many and great favours and blessings, I now, with a high sense of gratitude, presume to offer up my sincere thanks to the Almighty, the Creator and Preserver.
author: William Bartram

text: Alas, how quickly the gratitude owed to the dead flows off, how quick to be proved a deceiver.
author: Sophocles

text: Gratitude makes sense of our past, brings peace for today, and creates a vision for tomorrow.
author: Melody Beattie

text: The essence of all beautiful art, all great art, is gratitude.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: At times our own light goes out and is rekindled by a spark from another person. Each of us has cause to think with deep gratitude of those who have lighted the flame within us.
author: Albert Schweitzer

text: It is through gratitude for the present moment that the spiritual dimension of life opens up.
author: Eckhart Tolle

text: No one who achieves success does so without acknowledging the help of others. The wise and confident acknowledge this help with gratitude.
author: Alfred North Whitehead

text: Live a life full of humility, gratitude, intellectual curiosity, and never stop learning.
author: Gza

text: Joy is the simplest form of gratitude.
author: Karl Barth

text: Gratitude is the inward feeling of kindness received. Thankfulness is the natural impulse to express that feeling. Thanksgiving is the following of that impulse.
author: Henry Van Dyke

text: Revenge is profitable, gratitude is expensive.
author: Edward Gibbon

text: When a person doesn't have gratitude, something is missing in his or her humanity.
author: Elie Wiesel

text: Gratitude bestows reverence, allowing us to encounter everyday epiphanies, those transcendent moments of awe that change forever how we experience life and the world.
author: John Milton

text: Silent gratitude isn't much use to anyone.
author: Gertrude Stein

text: Gratitude changes the pangs of memory into a tranquil joy.
author: Dietrich Bonhoeffer

text: Sometimes we should express our gratitude for the small and simple things like the scent of the rain, the taste of your favorite food, or the sound of a loved one's voice.
author: Joseph B. Wirthlin

text: When you view your world with an attitude of gratitude, you are training yourself to focus on the good in life.
author: Paul J. Meyer

text: Gratitude is a duty which ought to be paid, but which none have a right to expect.
author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau

text: Nature's beauty is a gift that cultivates appreciation and gratitude.
author: Louie Schwartzberg

text: Gratitude is the most exquisite form of courtesy.
author: Jacques Maritain

text: Thankfulness is the beginning of gratitude. Gratitude is the completion of thankfulness. Thankfulness may consist merely of words. Gratitude is shown in acts.
author: Henri Frederic Amiel

text: Gratitude is when memory is stored in the heart and not in the mind.
author: Lionel Hampton

text: There is something about the first cup of coffee in the morning that feels like a small miracle - steam rising, warmth spreading through your hands, and the promise that today might be beautiful.
author: Anonymous

text: I'm grateful for the friends who stay when things get messy, who see me at my worst and choose to love me anyway.
author: Unknown

text: The sound of rain on the roof. The weight of a sleeping pet on your lap. The unexpected text from someone you've been thinking about. These are the moments that make life rich.
author: Anonymous

text: Some days, gratitude is simply noticing that you made it through. That you're still here, still trying, still hoping. And that alone is enough.
author: Unknown

text: I am grateful for laughter that catches you off guard, for tears that release what you've been holding, for all the ways your body knows how to heal.
author: Anonymous

text: The greatest gifts are often the smallest - a hand on your shoulder when you need it most, a smile from a stranger, the way sunlight finds its way through your window at just the right angle.
author: Unknown

text: There's a particular kind of magic in coming home to a space that feels like yours - where you can take off your armor, exhale deeply, and just be.
author: Anonymous

text: I am learning to be grateful for the closed doors, for the plans that fell apart, for all the times the universe said 'not yet' when I wanted 'right now.'
author: Unknown

text: Fresh sheets. A book that understands you. Music that speaks what you cannot say. Sometimes the most healing things are the simplest.
author: Anonymous

text: I'm grateful for the people who remember the little things - how you take your tea, what makes you laugh, the stories you've told before and would tell again.
author: Unknown

text: There is profound beauty in being seen - truly seen - by another person. Not the polished version of yourself, but the real, tender, messy you. That is a gift beyond measure.
author: Anonymous

text: Gratitude is waking up and realizing you have another day to try again, to do better, to love harder, to be gentler with yourself.
author: Unknown

text: The smell of bread baking. A child's laughter echoing down the street. The first star appearing at dusk. Pay attention - the world is constantly offering you small treasures.
author: Anonymous

text: I am grateful for every scar - not because the pain was worth it, but because I survived it. Each one is proof that I am stronger than I knew.
author: Unknown

text: There's something sacred about a moment of unexpected kindness - the stranger who holds the door, the friend who texts at exactly the right time, the way love shows up in the smallest gestures.
author: Anonymous

text: Tonight I am grateful for ordinary things: a full belly, a warm bed, a safe place to rest my head. What once felt like nothing now feels like everything.
author: Unknown

text: The best kind of gratitude isn't found in grand moments but in the quiet recognition that you are loved, that you matter, that your presence makes a difference.
author: Anonymous

text: I am grateful for second chances, for fresh starts, for all the mornings that whisper 'begin again' when yesterday felt too heavy to carry forward.
author: Unknown

text: There is sweetness in remembering that we are all just walking each other home - offering light when someone's gone dark, holding space when words run out, being present in the sacred ordinary.
author: Anonymous

text: Gratitude doesn't change the past, but it changes everything about how you carry it. It transforms your scars into stories, your pain into purpose, your survival into something beautiful.
author: Unknown

text: If good things lasted forever, would we appreciate how precious they are?
author: Bill Watterson

text: The gods envy us. They envy us because we're mortal, because any moment might be our last.
author: Achilles
